paragraphs: I build production machine learning systems — mostly speech. I was the first engineer hired at Ant Systemz; the technical team started the day I did, and I've since trained everyone who joined after me.

In that time I've taken an ASR training stack from an empty repository to distributed multi-GPU training running unattended on cloud instances, and written the founding commit of the dubbing product that is now the company's live application.

The work lives in an unglamorous middle layer I've grown fond of: the place where a model that works in a notebook has to survive four GPUs, a flaky NCCL collective, a three-day run that must resume exactly where it died, and a product surface that real people click on.
I came to this from full-stack web development, and it still shows — I'll happily go fix the React editor eating 4.5 GB of memory right after debugging a rendezvous hang.
